 Ty Jerome could turn into one of the most intriguing in-season trade targets available to hopeful NBA Title contenders. By Rucker Haringey | Oct 23, 2026, 2:50 PM EDT Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Orlando Magic v Memphis Grizzlies | Justin Ford/GettyImages Ty Jerome's 45-point outburst powered the Memphis Grizzlies to a nice Opening Night victory over the Utah Jazz. The veteran guard's sizzling play also reintroduced him to the rest of the league as one of the most intriguing potential in-season trade candidates that might be available to NBA title contenders.
--> Ty Jerome's 45-point outburst powered the Memphis Grizzlies to a nice Opening Night victory over the Utah Jazz. The veteran guard's sizzling play also reintroduced him to the rest of the league as one of the most intriguing potential in-season trade candidates that might be available to NBA title contenders.
 No one expects Jerome to remain one of the highest scoring guards in basketball, but it did show he still has the ability to be an elite 3-point marksman. What's more, Jerome also created his own shot against Utah which is a skill that only adds to his potential trade value for teams that need more offensive punch.

What's more, Jerome also created his own shot against Utah which is a skill that only adds to his potential trade value for teams that need more offensive punch.
 Of course, the Grizzlies also need every bit of Jerome's offensive skill if they want to compete for a playoff spot in the Western Conference this year. One of the biggest criticisms levided towards Memphis' roster is their lack of a top-end star who can carry their half court offense. Jerome is the team's best hope at having that kind of player on their roster in 2026-27. Jerome averaged 41.2 points and 11.9 assists per 100 possessions — no, seriously — while shooting 42.2 percent from 3. His 25.6 PER would have ranked him seventh in the league if he’d played enough minutes."

 The Grizzlies' front office will be in no hurry to move Jerome as long as they stay in the hunt. A potential core of Jerome, Zach Edey, and Cam Boozer could be enough to help Memphis find their way into the hunt for a postseason berth. A great percentage of those hopes do hinge on the health of Jerome and Edey. Injuries limited Jerome to just 15 games last year , and Edey's long-term health outlook is a big question mark after he missed so much action last season.

 Should the Grizzlies trade Ty Jerome?
--> Should the Grizzlies trade Ty Jerome?
 Memphis Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jerome's contract status is a big reason why the Grizzlies should strongly consider moving him via an in-season trade. This is the last guaranteed year of the contract he signed with Memphis in free agency. Next year Jerome has a player option for just under $10 million for the 2027-28 season that he will almost certainly decline, barring serious injury. 
--> Jerome's contract status is a big reason why the Grizzlies should strongly consider moving him via an in-season trade. This is the last guaranteed year of the contract he signed with Memphis in free agency. Next year Jerome has a player option for just under $10 million for the 2027-28 season that he will almost certainly decline, barring serious injury. 
 There's always a chance Memphis could try to tie Jerome down to a long-term deal, but that's a dangerous bet for a smaller guard who will be 30 before his next contract kicks in. That age also means Jerome is not a good fit on Memphis' potential timeline for real contention in the Western Conference.

That age also means Jerome is not a good fit on Memphis' potential timeline for real contention in the Western Conference.
 Jerome also projects to be one of the top non-superstars available in this season's trade market. The Grizzlies can take advantage of that tight market and Jerome's reasonable salary to extract a lot of value for him in a potential trade. There's a chance Memphis can extract a lottery pick or multiple first-rounders from a team that belives Jerome can help them win a championship.

There's a chance Memphis can extract a lottery pick or multiple first-rounders from a team that belives Jerome can help them win a championship.
 Add it all up, and trading Jerome is the right course for a Grizzlies organization that is methodically building around Boozer and Edey as their future core. Trading Jerome can help them accelerate that rebuild which should be the front office's top priority in the near future.
